terms.meaning: the markup language that describes the structure of a web page
style rules that control a web page's colors, spacing and layout
a Microsoft service for sharing company files online

depends_on: Backend API (called by the indexing function, not visible here)
used_by: launcher.py (opens this file in the browser)

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Base page styling
sections.what: Declares the page type and title, then sets the base look: fonts, a purple background, a white centered card, and the main heading styles.
sections.why: Likely reason: a consistent look without loading outside style files. Reason not stated.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Form input and button styling
sections.what: Styles the text boxes, the multi-line box, the buttons with their hover and press effects, a green alternative button, and the result box.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Whether the green alternative button is used is not visible in the shown part.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Answer, source and loading styles
sections.what: Styles the answer box, each source citation and its links, the spinning loading indicator, and the status message area.
sections.why: Likely reason: a visible spinner tells users a slow search is still running. Reason not stated.

sections.name: File setup (part 4)
sections.title: Notice styles and first form
sections.what: Colors the success and error messages, styles the how-to box, then shows the header and the form where a user types a folder and a collection name and presses Index Folder.
sections.why: Likely reason: the first step must be done before questions work, so it is shown first. The on-page note supports this.
sections.watch_out: The folder hint mentions SharePoint while the launcher selects a local folder, and the collection default differs from the launcher's default.

sections.name: File setup (part 5)
sections.title: Question box and action buttons
sections.what: Draws the question step: a text box and three buttons labelled Get Answer, Export to Excel and Email Results. It also contains the hidden email form, the loading message and the answer area.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page is one plain HTML file, so each step of the form is written out in order.
sections.watch_out: The email form is shown and hidden by script, so renaming its element ids would break the Send Email button.

sections.name: File setup (part 6)
sections.title: Index folder and send question
sections.what: Finishes the folder indexing step, which asks the server to read the documents in the folder, then starts the question step. That step sends the typed question and collection name to the server and places the returned answer on the page.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page calls the server directly with fetch, so the user does not need a separate app.
sections.watch_out: The answer text is placed on the page as raw HTML, so document text containing HTML tags could change how the page looks.

sections.name: File setup (part 7)
sections.title: Show sources and start Excel export
sections.what: Builds the list of sources under the answer, showing file name, page, slide or sheet, a SharePoint link when available, and a relevance percentage. Also finishes the Excel export by downloading the result with a dated file name.
sections.why: Likely reason: the sources list lets the user check where each part of the answer came from.
sections.watch_out: File names from the server are placed on the page as raw HTML, so an unusual file name could break the layout.

sections.name: File setup (part 8)
sections.title: Email form and sending
sections.what: Shows and hides the email form. When the user sends, it posts the question, answer and sources to the server, which is asked to send them through Outlook. After success, the email boxes are cleared.
sections.why: Likely reason: the browser cannot send Outlook email itself, so the server is asked to do it.
sections.watch_out: Email is sent by the server, so the server must be running and Outlook must be installed and open on the machine where the server runs.

sections.name: File setup (part 9)
sections.title: Error for email and startup check
sections.what: Shows an error message if sending email fails. When the page opens, it asks the server whether it is running and shows a green or red message.
sections.why: Likely reason: the owner sees at once whether the server is running, instead of finding out only when a button fails.
sections.watch_out: The startup check uses a fixed address, so if the server runs on a different port the page always reports that the server is not running.

summary: The search web page's styling and the start of its layout, showing the instructions and the first step of indexing a folder. Only part of the file was shown.
purpose: Gives the search page its look and the forms a user fills in to index documents and ask questions.
why: Likely reason: one self-contained page can open directly from the launcher without a web server. Reason not stated.
how: Style rules set colors, spacing, boxes, buttons, the loading spinner and status messages. The page body begins with a header, a how-to box, a status area and the Index Folder form. The form's button calls a script function that is not in the shown part. The remaining sections were not shown, so the full flow is not visible.
inputs: A folder path and a collection name that the user types into the form.
outputs: The visual page. Pressing Index Folder calls a function whose behavior is not visible here.
risks: The button calls a function whose code is not in the shown part. The folder hint mentions SharePoint, but the launcher picks a local folder. The collection hint says the default is default, while the launcher uses my_documents.
debug: If the button does nothing, check the indexing function in the rest of the file and the browser's developer console. If the page looks broken, check the style rules at the top.
